response.rationale: The fluctuant mass and focal tenderness specifically along the flexor sheath, with limited digit motion, point to pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis rather than diffuse cellulitis or joint-based septic arthritis. Radiographs show intact bony anatomy, arguing against septic arthritis.

rejected.why: Septic arthritis would involve joint inflammation, but the findings are localized to the flexor sheath and radiographs show intact bony anatomy with no joint-specific destruction.
Cellulitis is a diffuse skin/soft-tissue infection, whereas the exam shows a localized fluctuant mass and tenderness over the flexor sheath, indicating tenosynovitis.
